Sources & facilitation guide

This public policy review can be explored individually or facilitated as a group discussion. It does not depend on any prior assignment. Allow students to debate before following a witness or making a decision. No selection is graded right or wrong. The eight illustrated places at the top show your route: choose a visited stop to rewind to that decision; any later choices on that route are cleared.

What is established?

The four original Aldovia scenario passages are reproduced verbatim from the provided teaching materials. The Finance Ministry reports lower expenditure and deficit, and no decline in recorded GDP; other effects emerge in subsequent scenes. The illustrations, fictional witnesses, committee deliberations, and hypothetical outcomes are learning devices, not historical evidence or statements by Diane Elson.

Source audit: Introduction to The Diane Elson Reader

    Questions to keep alive

    Has the government reduced the real work required, or shifted its costs? What can the reports show, and what remains causally uncertain? Whose time, entitlements, and voices count? How can a policy reduce and redistribute unpaid work rather than merely count it? Which fiscal constraints are decisions rather than immutable facts?

    How to facilitate

    Suggested time: 35–55 minutes. In small groups, ask students to defend at least one interpretation that they initially oppose. For the policy proposal, discuss choices as tradeoffs. The menus do not substitute for the conversation: the class must give reasons and can add its own qualification. Rewind through the illustrated places to test a different interpretation.
